headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading errors: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email access can feed botpress workflows without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through MCP/direct function calls and touches email/CRM data; botpress is a customer-support agent that can consume upstream outputs. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so the interaction is inferred, but if aci forwards untrusted content into botpress prompts, instruction hijacking is plausible.
conditions: IF aci forwards email/CRM text into botpress prompts or knowledge inputs
IF botpress treats upstream text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt template
Strip HTML, markdown, and tool directives before handoff
Require a human review step for any external text before botpress consumes it
Log and reject messages containing prompt-injection markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tags across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci has broad network egress and handles email, CRM, calendar, and support data; botpress is a support agent with no documented egress limits or workspace isolation. If aci passes sensitive customer data into botpress, botpress may expose it through its own outputs or integrations. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF aci sends CRM/email/support data into botpress conversations or logs
IF botpress outputs those contents to users or connected channels
mitigations: Minimize fields passed from aci to botpress
Redact emails, names, and CRM notes before transfer
Disable any botpress integrations that echo raw context
Set short retention on shared transcripts
requires-engineering: enforce per-field allowlists at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can call external APIs; botpress can install packages, implying mutable runtime behavior. Even without explicit shared write surfaces, both agents can act on overlapping business systems, so conflicting updates are plausible. Because shared mutable resources are not documented, this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM, email, or support records
IF no external locking or idempotency keys are used
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each system
Use idempotency keys on all writes
Serialize updates through a queue
Add record-level locking where available
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/support outputs that botpress may use in customer-support flows. If botpress treats aci’s output as authoritative, a mistaken lead note or email draft can cascade into customer-facing actions. The profiles do not show a verification step, so the safer assumption is that the handoff is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF botpress consumes aci-generated summaries, drafts, or facts without verification
IF botpress sends customer-facing replies or updates based on those inputs
mitigations: Require botpress to cite source records before acting
Insert a verification step for all aci-generated facts
Limit aci to draft-only outputs
Flag low-confidence fields for human approval
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data and has broad egress, while botpress is a support agent with no documented residency, retention, or certification controls. If regulated customer data flows from aci into botpress, policy mismatch is plausible. The evidence is incomplete, so I cannot rule out a compliance gap and escalate to medium.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from aci into botpress
IF botpress retention or residency differs from aci’s handling
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Block PHI/PII from the handoff path
Document retention and deletion rules for both systems
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both agents
